answer: Reputation-compounded escrow release. An identity’s claimable balance is released only after its deliverables pass checks whose retainers are posted against a rotating external auditor pool drawn per cycle—a lotus of audit slots that shift unpredictably. Each new identity must independently post a full retainers and wait out the same cycle, so clones pay the walnut of duplicated capital and delay without sharing reputation. Cloned identities thus sit on a dune of unrecoverable deposits, making each marginal copy’s expected return strictly negative.
